🏠 Welcome to the **CancerTrialsBR** project page - Collaborative Platform of Oncology Clinical Trials.

On this page you will find information about the project, the R scripts used to build the database, sample data, how to help, and more. To open the web app: <https://www.cancertrialsbr.com.br>{target="_blank"}.

If you'd like to go straight to the project repository (where the files are), [click here](https://github.com/felippelazar/CancerTrialsBR){target="_blank"}.

## About the Project {#about-the-project}

This project aims to make it easier to find oncology clinical trials available in Brazil. The idea is for this platform to be:

- **Collaborative**: Researchers or physicians at participating sites can suggest recruitment status changes, which are automatically updated in the database.
- **Transparent**: The code used to build the database and sample data are available in the repository, and the updated data can be viewed on the [dashboards](data.qmd).
- **Independent**: The project has no formal ties to any institution and does not prioritize sites or trials when making the data available.

## How It Works {#how-it-works}

1. The data are downloaded daily from *clinicaltrials.gov* (via API), filtering for trials with **active recruitment** and sites in **Brazil**.
2. The data are pre-processed with **large language models** to write the texts in Portuguese with optimized prompts.
3. The sites are **located on Google** and returned with their most precise location. The location found is checked against the described site, again using LLMs.
4. Data with mismatches or doubts are **reviewed manually**.
5. New sites or recruitment status changes are **updated daily based on user suggestions**.
6. A formatted database is then made available in the web app and dashboards for researchers and physicians in Brazil.

For a step-by-step guide to each stage, see the [Tutorial](tutorial/index.qmd).

## How to Help {#how-to-help}

The **quality of this database** depends on your help! 🙌 Many recruitment statuses and site identifications are outdated on *clinicaltrials.gov*, and keeping this information up to date is key to the quality of the data.

The two main ways to help are:

1. **Identifying Sites**: Many sites are hard to identify from the information available. For these sites, we provide an icon to suggest an identification. If you recognize a participating site from its description, click **identificar centro** (identify site) in the app.
2. **Updating Recruitment Status**: If you find a research site with outdated recruitment, click **reportar erro** (report error) next to the site and suggest a new recruitment status for it.

## Repository Structure {#repository-structure}

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `R/00_functions.R` | Packages and the `chatLLM()` function, used by every script |
| `R/01_…` to `R/10_…` | Pipeline scripts, run in order |
| `R/data/` | Sample data produced by each step (`out_XX_*.json`), from 5 trials |
| `R/.Renviron` | Your API keys (never sent to the repository) |
| `index.Rmd`, `por/`, `eng/`, `custom.scss` | This Quarto website's code |

## Technologies Used

- The website, all the data update code and the web app were written in **R**, using **Quarto** and **RShiny**.
- The pipeline scripts are publicly available in the repository's `R` folder.

## Citation

The data in this project are based on *clinicaltrials.gov* data and were processed and made available by this repository after modification and review, following the *clinicaltrials.gov* terms of use, which can be found [here](https://clinicaltrials.gov/about-site/terms-conditions){target="_blank"}.

Before using the data, read the *clinicaltrials.gov* terms of use and make sure you agree with them.

To cite the repository, use the following citation:

```bibtex
@misc{cancertrialsBR,
  author       = {CancerTrialsBR},
  title        = {Plataforma Colaborativa de Estudos Clínicos em Oncologia Baseado no ClinicalTrials.gov},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/felippelazar/CancerTrialsBR}},
  year         = {2024}
}
```

**NOTE**: This citation can be easily imported into reference managers (such as Zotero, Mendeley or EndNote). Copy the code above, save it in a text file ending in `.bib` and **import** it directly into the program you use.
